objective.statement: Group notes neatly so that every beat can be seen, in 2/2, 3/2, 4/2 and 3/8.
successCriteria: I know to beam quavers and semiquavers within a beat.
I know a minim beat can hold four quavers beamed together.
I can fix a bar whose beams hide the beats.

explanation.text: Beams join short notes together. Good grouping shows where each beat is, so that a bar is easy to read at a glance.
The rule is the same as in Grade 1: group the notes of one beat together, and do not join across the next beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/2: four beamed quavers, then two crotchets.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 4 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver), crotchet, crotchet.

explanation.caption: In 2/2 the beat is a minim. Four quavers fill one minim beat, so they are beamed together as one group.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 3/8: three pairs of beamed semiquavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 2 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver), 2 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver), 2 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver).

explanation.caption: In 3/8 each beat is a quaver, which holds two semiquavers. Each beat is one beamed pair.

explanation.text: Notes that are not shorter than a crotchet have no beams. Beams only appear on quavers and shorter.
Ask: where does each beat start and end? Keep each beam inside its own beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/2: two crotchets, then four beamed quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, crotchet, 4 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver).

steps: The first beat is a minim's worth: two crotchets.
The second beat is a minim's worth: four quavers, joined by one beam.
Each beat can be seen separately, so the bar is easy to read.

feedback.correct: Yes: that bar shows each beat.

mistakes.bar-overfull: This bar holds more beats than the time signature allows. Count the beats again and remove the extra.
mistakes.bar-underfull: There's still room in this bar. Count how many beats are missing.
mistakes.grouping-obscures-beat: The beats add up, but it's hard to see where each beat starts. Regroup the notes so every beat is visible.
mistakes.unnecessary-tie: You can write those tied notes as a single note (or a dotted note). That's easier to read.
mistakes.rest-grouping: Each silent beat (or part-beat) normally gets its own rest. Split the silence along the beats.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Check the beat total first, then how the notes are grouped.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.
